name: Petter Dass
credit: Alleged portrait of Petter Dass, unknown artist (c. 1684), Melhus church · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Petter Dass (1647–1707) was a Lutheran priest and the foremost Norwegian poet of his generation. Born on the island of Herøy in Nordland, he served as a parish priest at Alstahaug in Helgeland from 1689 until his death, and wrote in the Danish-Norwegian of his day, with many words of the Nordland coast.

He is best known for Nordlands Trompet, a topographical poem in rhymed six-line stanzas that describes the weather, fish, birds, people and parishes of northern Norway. It circulated in manuscript and was not printed until 1739, but became widely loved, and his hymns also remained in use for generations.
